newsitem.title: USA: CME's Sandner sells his stake in IFOA broker group.
newsitem.headline: CME's Sandner sells his stake in IFOA broker group.

text.p: Chicago Mercantile Exchange chairman Jack Sandner said he had sold his nine percent stake in one of the CME's largest broker groups, International Futures & Options Associates (IFOA).
"I sold my share in the floor brokerage association IFOA last week," Sandner told Reuters Monday after a news conference on Chicago's financial services industry.
Broker groups or associations consist of two or more floor brokers who share profits or expenses as a way to pool costs from trading losses and other overhead expenses.

Sandner said he sold his share to James Kaulentis, the managing partner of IFOA, after Kaulentis was fined $10,000 and suspended from the exchange floor for 30 days in late November for fighting with another member.
As managing partner, Kaulentis oversees some 66 brokers in the CME's trading pits.
"In this particular case there was a fight, which sort of upset me because I have a nine percent interest in the association," Sandner said. "That was the catalyst."
Kaulentis said Sandner's sale had been under negotiation for over a year. He said tax-related problems that have since been resolved, coupled with his fine and suspension, led to the sale last week.
Neither Kaulentis nor Sandner would elaborate on the terms of the sale.
"He has no ownership interests at all," Kaulentis said. "He was an outside investor and I never discussed business with him."
Sandner denied industry speculation that half of his futures commission merchant firm RB&H Financial Group Inc was up for sale.
"No, it's not for sale," said Sander, who is president of RB&H.
Sandner owns 51 percent of RB&H, and Dearborn Financial Group and Traco International own 49 percent. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
